title: Targeted Gene Manipulation and Thermogenic Evaluation in Mouse Brown Adipocytes
author: Bunk, Soni, et al.
materials: Stericup Quick Release-HV Sterile Vacuum Filtration System

28.Brown adipocyte isolation (this protocol uses 5 mice):a.Euthanize mice by direct cervical dislocation and excise interscapular brown adipose tissue (iBAT). Keep iBAT immersed in cold PBS until all samples are collected.b.Blot excess PBS with a Kimtech wipe to dry pooled iBAT tissue.c.Transfer tissues into a 10 mL glass beaker and finely mince using spring scissors for ∼7 min.d.Transfer minced tissue into 10 mL of digestion buffer in a 50 mL conical tube.e.Shake at 150 rpm in a 37°C water bath for 50 min. Vortex for 2 s every 5 min during digestion.f.Pass the digested suspension through a 100 μm cell strainer into a 50 mL tube containing 10 mL stop buffer (4 mM EDTA, pH 8.0; 3% BSA in PBS).g.Gently invert the tube three times and incubate upright at 20–25°C for 40 min to allow adipocytes to float.h.Using a plastic Pasteur pipette, collect the fat layer and transfer it into a fresh 15 mL tube containing 10 mL DMEM/F12 GlutaMAX + 10% FBS.Note: Aspirate slowly. Avoid transferring clumped white fat.i.Invert the 15 mL tube gently three times and incubate upright for 40 min at 20°C–25°C to allow adipocytes to float again.j.Collect the brown adipocyte layer and transfer into a 5 mL tube containing 2 mL fresh DMEM/F12 GlutaMAX + 10% FBS.29.Assessment of brown adipocyte number:a.Gently invert the 5 mL tube three times to distribute cells evenly.b.Using a wide-bore pipette tip, load 10 μL of adipocyte suspension into a Bright-Line Hemocytometer (Hausser Scientific).c.Count only multilocular adipocytes (see white arrows in Figure 4).
CRITICAL: If concentration exceeds 300,000 adipocytes/mL, dilute the sample and recount.
Note: Viability stains may be used to distinguish live cells from dead cells; however, in our experience, dyes like trypan blue are hard to detect due to the small cytoplasmic area because of lipid droplets.
30.Measuring oxygen consumption of brown adipocytes: Set up and calibrate the Clark-type electrode (Rank Brothers) as previously described.15
a.Add DMEM/F12 + 10% FBS to the electrode chamber.b.Allow equilibration with atmospheric oxygen until a stable signal is obtained.Note: Rate at this stage reflects electrode drift.Note: Electrode drift should not exceed 1% O2 per 5 min.Note: Excessive noise indicates improper setup and requires electrode reassembly.c.Add 10,000 brown adipocytes to the chamber (final volume = 0.7 mL, 37°C).d.Seal the chamber with a plunger.e.Record basal respiration (prior to drug addition) for 30–60 s once the trace stabilizes.CRITICAL: Use only the linear portion of the basal trace.f.Add thermogenic activators or inhibitors via a Hamilton syringe to the stirring chamber.Note: A transient change in O2% may occur upon needle insertion; allow 15–30 s for stabilization.g.Ensure that different treatment groups are measured using the same electrodes to control for electrode-specific variability.h.Acquire data using the Rank Brothers Dual Digital Model 20 with PicoLog 6 software.31.Data analysis:Note: Quantify OCR using the linear region of each trace (see Figure 5).a.Export data as “%O2 vs time (s)” from PicoLog 6 (.csv format).b.Import into OriginPro 2025 (or GraphPad Prism) for best-fit line analysis.c.Determine slope values representing rate of O2 consumption (%O2 s-1).Example Parameters.i.Electrode Drift: before cell addition (stabilized electrode).ii.Basal Respiration: post-cell addition, before drugs.iii.Drug-driven Respiration: after compound addition.d.Calculate oxygen consumption rate (OCR) per 106 cells using:OCR(nmolesO2min−1·10−6cells)=−m×2.4×V×60×1,000,000cm: rate of O2 consumption (%O2 s-1).V: total reaction volume (mL) in chamber.c: number of brown adipocytes in chamber.

steps.title: Plasmid preparation for AAV vector
steps.instruction: Transform DH5α E. coli with pAAV-CA-FLEX plasmid, incubate on selective agar at 37 °C with shaking for 8–12 h, harvest colonies, purify plasmid DNA using a midi‑ or maxi‑prep kit, and verify plasmid integrity by whole‑plasmid sequencing (e.g., Plasmidsaurus).

steps.title: HEK293T cell seeding and PEI stock
steps.instruction: Seed HEK293T/17 cells in a 15 cm dish containing DMEM + 10 % FBS + 1 % Penicillin‑Streptomycin; allow cells to reach 90–100 % confluence, changing medium every 48 h; prepare PEI (25 kDa) stock by dissolving PEI to 1 mg mL⁻¹ in water at 60 °C, aliquot, and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Transfect HEK293T cells for AAV production

substeps.instruction: a. Seed HEK293T/17 cells in 15‑cm dishes with DMEM + 10 % FBS + 1 % Pen/Strep and keep in a humidified incubator at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ until ≥90 % confluent.
b. Three hours before transfection replace medium with 25 mL DMEM + 5 % FBS + 1 % Pen/Strep.

c. Prepare the transfection cocktail in OptiMEM (total 2.5 mL): add 10 µg pAAV-CA-FLEX_GFP‑FLAG (final 3.7 µg mL⁻¹), 39.5 µg pDP8.ape (AAV8) (final 14.6 µg mL⁻¹), and 200 µL PEI (final 74.1 µg mL⁻¹). Mix by inverting and incubate 10–15 min at 20–25 °C; avoid freeze‑thawing PEI and add PEI last to prevent DNA precipitation.
d. Add the transfection mix dropwise to the cells and return to the incubator.
e. After 24 h replace the medium with 20 mL DMEM + 10 % FBS + 1 % Pen/Strep.
f. Continue incubation for an additional 48 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Harvest and purify AAV particles
steps.instruction: Collect and purify AAV from cells and media:

substeps.instruction: a. Scrape cells from two 15‑cm dishes together with their culture medium into one 50 mL tube.
b. Centrifuge 15 min at 3,000 × g, 4 °C; discard pellet.
c. Filter the supernatant through a 0.45 µm Stericup filter.
d. Aliquot 40 mL filtered media into clean 50 mL tubes.
e. Add 10 mL pre‑chilled 5× AAV concentration reagent to each 40 mL aliquot, invert five times, and incubate at 4 °C for at least 24 h (do not exceed 5 days).
f. Centrifuge 30 min at 1,500 × g, 4 °C; a whitish pellet of viral particles will form.
g. Resuspend the pellet in 300–400 µL sterile PBS.
h. Aliquot the virus suspension into small volumes as needed, flash‑freeze in liquid nitrogen, and store at –80 °C.
i. Preserve two‑to‑three 5 µL aliquots in separate 1.5 mL tubes for future titration.

steps.title: Prepare Krebs‑Ringer bicarbonate buffer (KRBMB)
steps.instruction: Make KRBMB at the following final concentrations: NaCl 135 mM, KCl 5 mM, CaCl₂ 1 mM, MgCl₂ 1 mM, K₂HPO₄ 0.4 mM, NaHPO₄ 25 mM, HEPES 20 mM. Store at 4 °C for up to one month.

steps.title: Prepare digestion buffer for adipocyte isolation
steps.instruction: For digestion of tissue from five mice, combine KRBMB with: Collagenase B 2 mg mL⁻¹, Soybean Trypsin Inhibitor 1 mg mL⁻¹, D‑Glucose 10 mM, and 20 % fatty‑acid‑free BSA (0.22 µm‑filtered) diluted to 4 % (add 2 mL). Prepare fresh on the day of the experiment.

steps.title: Isolate brown adipocytes from mouse iBAT

substeps.instruction: a. Euthanize mice by direct cervical dislocation and excise interscapular brown adipose tissue (iBAT); keep tissue immersed in cold PBS.
b. Blot excess PBS with a Kimtech wipe and transfer pooled iBAT to a 10 mL glass beaker.
c. Finely mince the tissue with spring scissors for ~7 min.
d. Transfer minced tissue to 10 mL digestion buffer in a 50 mL conical tube.
e. Shake at 150 rpm in a 37 °C water bath for 50 min, vortexing 2 s every 5 min.
f. Pass the digested suspension through a 100 µm cell strainer into a 50 mL tube containing 10 mL stop buffer (4 mM EDTA, pH 8.0; 3 % BSA in PBS).
g. Invert the tube three times and incubate upright at 20–25 °C for 40 min to allow adipocytes to float.
h. Using a plastic Pasteur pipette, slowly collect the floating fat layer and transfer it to a fresh 15 mL tube with 10 mL DMEM/F12 GlutaMAX + 10 % FBS.
i. Invert the 15 mL tube gently three times and incubate upright for another 40 min at 20–25 °C.
j. Collect the brown adipocyte layer and transfer it to a 5 mL tube containing 2 mL fresh DMEM/F12 GlutaMAX + 10 % FBS.
a. Gently invert the 5 mL tube three times to distribute cells evenly.
b. Load 10 µL of the suspension into a Bright‑Line hemocytometer using a wide‑bore pipette tip.
c. Count only multilocular adipocytes; if the concentration exceeds 300,000 adipocytes mL⁻¹, dilute the sample and recount.

steps.title: Calibrate Clark‑type oxygen electrode
steps.instruction: Set up and calibrate the electrode:

substeps.instruction: a. Add DMEM/F12 + 10 % FBS to the electrode chamber.
b. Allow equilibration with atmospheric oxygen until a stable signal is obtained; electrode drift must be ≤1 % O₂ per 5 min.
c. If excessive noise is observed, re‑assemble the electrode before proceeding.

steps.title: Measure oxygen consumption of brown adipocytes

substeps.instruction: a. Add 10,000 brown adipocytes to the chamber (final volume 0.7 mL) and maintain at 37 °C.
b. Seal the chamber with a plunger.
c. Record basal respiration for 30–60 s once the trace stabilizes; use only the linear portion of the basal trace.
d. Add thermogenic activators or inhibitors via a Hamilton syringe to the stirring chamber.
e. Allow 15–30 s for signal stabilization after needle insertion.
f. Ensure that all treatment groups are measured with the same electrode to control for electrode‑specific variability.
g. Acquire data using the Rank Brothers Dual Digital Model 20 with PicoLog 6 software.

steps.title: Analyze respiration data and calculate OCR

substeps.instruction: a. Export the data as “%O₂ vs time (s)” in .csv format from PicoLog 6.
b. Import the file into OriginPro 2025 (or GraphPad Prism) and perform a best‑fit line analysis on the linear region of each trace.

c. Determine the slope (m) representing %O₂ s⁻¹ and calculate oxygen consumption rate per 10⁶ cells using: OCR (nmol O₂ min⁻¹ · 10⁻⁶ cells) = –m × 2.4 × V × 60 × 1,000,000 / c, where V is the total reaction volume (mL) in the chamber and c is the number of brown adipocytes in the chamber.
